messages.author: b98ebc0e292a4fb2
messages.subject: SpectronauttoMSstats column error
parts:
Hi Everyone, I am looking for diffrentially expressed proteins between two groups (healthy and disease), my experiments were analyzed using Spectronaut so I tried using SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat to convert my csv file to Msstats format but I keep getting this error message in R;
> sStatconverted_data <- MSstatsConvert::SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(spectronaut_data)INFO  [2025-01-08 02:05:34] ** Raw data from Spectronaut imported successfully.Error in data.table::setnames(spec_input, c("PGProteinGroups", "EGModifiedSequence",  :   'old' is length 8 but 'new' is length 9

I believe the error is from a mismatch between the number of columns in my Spectronaut data and what the SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat function expects.  I tried to look up for an example of what my spectronaut output file should include to match MSstats but couldn't find any leads.  The column headers of my spectronaut output csv file are;


R.Condition


 R.FileName


 R.Replicate


  PG.ProteinAccessions


  PG.ProteinDescriptions


   PG.ProteinGroups


    PG.Cscore


     PG.Cscore (Run-Wise)


       PG.Pvalue


      PG.PValue (Run-Wise)


      PG.Qvalue


  PG.QValue (Run-Wise)


   PG.RunEvidenceCount   


PG.MS1Quantity


    PG.Quantity


     PEP.GroupingKey


        PEP.GroupingKeyType


       PEP.IsProteotypic


    PEP.NrOfMissedCleavages


     PEP.StrippedSequence


         PEP.Rank


   PEP.RunEvidenceCount


   PEP.UsedForProteinGroupQuantity


  FG.Charge


   FG.IntMID


  FG.LabeledSequence


  FG.PrecMz


    FG.PrecMzCalibrated


    FG.Quantity

 Also I am not sure if I need the annotation file and how to create it? 

So, I am kind of lost from where to start. I would appreciate any information or feedback that you can give me or if there is any resources or tutorial I can follow  that would help.

 

Also these are the documentation link I followed with their R script;

https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/MSstats/inst/doc/MSstatsWorkflow.html?fbclid=IwY2xjawHqDnBleHRuA2FlbQIxMAABHfHrT2nAaDDHDtAv6bY_qhErTuEzj9KgLAUFs_iKSWlxqPC_uOyLWHtehA_aem_rhRVAjda7gC0ZmQ3FD5oIg 


thanks a lot :)
